H.title: Selection acquires the selector grant after the assessor grant set, violating the global sorted order
H.status: CONFIRMED source defect; PostgreSQL interleaving not executed
H.scenario: Selection readiness calls load_run_observations, which FOR UPDATE-locks the sorted narrative-assessor grants. The selector is absent from that set unless also an assessor. Later custodian.admit locks the selector grant separately. For disjoint master sets in the same project, selection S can hold assessor Z's grant and wait for selector A's grant. A concurrent A6 disposition on the other master set, issued by A with assessor Z, takes the correct sorted union A then Z: it holds A and waits for Z. This is a cycle. Two selections with exchanged selector/assessor roles can also cycle. Profile FOR SHARE locks are compatible and disjoint masters do not serialize these writers. Current fixtures use one actor and common masters, masking this case.
H.fix: Before readiness_in, at the grant-head position after the packaging head, call lock_grant_heads once over {request.command.actor_id} union human_principals for the bound run, as A6 does. Every later grant check must re-take only this already locked set. Add barrier-controlled PostgreSQL tests with distinct principals and disjoint master sets for selection versus A6 and selection versus selection, observing the intended waiter.

M.title: C6 is implemented at preview creation but omitted at the selection boundary
M.status: CONFIRMED missing verification; no ordinary append-only writer bypass claimed
M.scenario: After loading a digest-valid preview, select reloads the run and disposition but never reloads the exact M8 revision or PackagingObservation. It never re-runs candidate payload/closure/lineage verification, compares the observation body to the preview's observation digest and profile constraint snapshot, or rechecks variant/waiver coverage. A corrupt candidate or packaging observation after preview creation can therefore be newly selected while run/disposition readiness remains intact. Normal append-only triggers prevent ordinary updates, but the explicitly carried C6 requirement is fail-closed verification at every consuming boundary, including selection/load; cached historical preview data is not that verification. Repository selection load verifies the receipt and embedded preview digest only.
M.fix: Share an exact package-evidence resolver between preview and fresh selection: load the pinned revision, recompute payload and both closures, verify lineage against the bound run/profile, load and verify the observation and its exact run/candidate/snapshot binding, compare its recomputed digest with the preview, then validate chosen variants and waivers. Use it before appending a fresh selection. Keep historical replay semantics explicit. Add candidate/lineage/observation tamper-after-preview tests proving no selection/head advancement.

M.title: B3 writer-pair tests do not establish the required blocked-waiter interleavings
M.scenario: The selection/disposition and selection/selection tests merely gather tasks. They contain no barriers, no observed PostgreSQL blocked waiter, and no queued FOR UPDATE behind FOR SHARE assertion. They can pass with effectively serial execution. There is no selection/run-seal or profile-publication/selection test in this file. Thus newer-run rejection and publication/currentness serialization, and both writer orders, lack the design's required proof. Same-master no-op UPDATE locking can serialize these fixtures before the interesting head/grant locks are reached.
M.fix: Add deterministic real-PG selection x run seal, selection x disposition, profile publication x selection and selection x selection tests with explicit barriers and pg lock/waiter observations, covering both commit orders, refusal after a competing head wins, and a queued FOR UPDATE behind FOR SHARE. Include the disjoint-master/multiple-principal case from H1. Keep export pairs scheduled for B4 rather than claiming them in B3.

M.title: Selection RED coverage omits the central lease, waiver, expiry and currentness refusal cases
M.scenario: The test named unwaived_blocking_findings_and_stray_waivers_are_refused only exercises a stray waiver against the clean observation. It does not exercise FAIL, allowed exact waivers, incomplete/extra/wrong-rule coverage, or an unwaivable BLOCKING rule. The suite also lacks changed request/preview lease binding, expired lease and preview, grant revocation/change after lease issuance, API-key refusal, invalid group choices, stale master/profile/newer run, target-slot confusion, selection-command conflict, concurrent identical-command replay and crash-after-lease assertions. Existing pure tests check window shapes and canonicalization, not these DB-time service decisions. A6 tests cover A6 implementations and cannot prove this separate copied custodian/service.
M.fix: Persist focused service tests for these B3 refusal paths and a valid multi-group/waived selection. Assert no selection or head advancement on every refusal, distinguish preview versus disposition versus lease expiry using DB-time seams, verify the same lease cannot authorize changed choices/waivers, and test historical replay versus a changed body under the same selection command.

Selection takes master write locks, profile FOR SHARE, run/disposition FOR SHARE, preview FOR UPDATE and packaging advisory/head FOR UPDATE in the stated order. Profile publication takes its head FOR UPDATE before grants; A6 takes run FOR SHARE and disposition exclusive before grants. A5 first takes a run advisory and later takes the actual run-head FOR UPDATE in append_run; identical-subject writers also serialize on master authority locks. Do not treat the design shorthand as evidence that A5 locks its row before every grant check, or claim queued-mode/deadlock proof without the required PG interleavings. H1's late selector grant violates the sorted grant-set invariant independently.
